programme.title: Hunting with a Lost Lemming: Okayest Hunter's 2022 deer hunting season kickoff!
programme.desc:
The crew from the Okayest Hunter podcast thought it'd be a good idea to start a hunting show, but they wanted to do something different, and it needed to align with the brand, mission, and ethos of the Okayest Hunter. Basically, it can't be too serious. So we thought, hey, let's make the "Office" show, but for hunting.
Our hunting season is chock full of humility as we miss place things, take too long to pick out our tree, injure ourselves, miss deer, lose arrows, and more. However, we had one of our best and most fun seasons yet! Follow along as we release new episodes as our 2022 deer hunting season unfolds. We assure you it'll be worth getting all the way to the end!
Cheers to chasing shooter bucks in the deer woods and never passing on what makes you happy! We hope you can relate as we share our shenanigans with everyone!
Okayest Hunter Show, season one: We'll See How it Goes, Episode one: Hunting with a lost lemming.

programme.title: Ghost Stories, Crayfish of Unusual Size and Turkey Invasions
programme.desc: On this episode of Outdoor Weekly we have ghosts? Aliens? Bigfoot? Escaped government experiment looking to exact revenge on those that condemned it to a life of torment and misery? We also have a North Dakota man who thinks he broke the state record for walleye but it is disqualified for one key reason. A Pennsylvania man who DOES break a state record for catfish and no he didn't use mousefish as bait. Crayfish, crawfish, crawdad, it doesn't matter what you call it, a water plant worker found a MASSIVE specimen that could have been mistaken for a lobster. A new gang is stirring up trouble in a rural town – a gang of turkeys are terrorizing residents. And last but not least, we check in with the beautiful Jana Waller to give us updates on this year's bear season.

programme.title: Don't Miss
programme.desc: Watch this cinematic adventure as Paul Lawver and Joel Port hit public land on the Eastern Shore of Maryland chasing Sika a.k.a. the elusive marsh ghosts. Sika deer (technically a species of the elk family) were released in the swamps of Maryland in the early 1900's. Sika originate from Thailand/Japan/East Asia and have flourished in Maryland so well, their season co-insides with whitetail yet have their own separate bag limits.

programme.title: Slow down for more birds
programme.desc:
You set the pace in the field, and if you're in a rush so is your dog. That means less time in a scent cone and more missed birds.
Scott Linden of Wingshooting USA TV shows you how, and explains why, you should dial things down a bit when it comes to covering a field or covert.
If you want more tips on dog training and bird hunting, go to: www.findbirdhuntingspots.com

programme.title: Hunting dog tailgate exam, part one
programme.desc:
Your best hunting partner needs some TLC ... especially after a hunt. wingshooting USA TV host Scott Linden provides the first part of three, helping you check him from nose tip to tail and ensure he's healthy, safe, and ready to go the next day.
Today, it's all about your dog's coat. We'll cover why it's important to get him off the ground, how "training" for the exam is critical, and what to look for from injuries to parasites. Your dog will stay healthier, well-rested, and ready to go the next day.
You'll also see some fun and exciting bird hunting footage from a hunt where the tailgate exam became crucial.

programme.title: Take a newcomer hunting - here's how
programme.desc:
Safety first, but then what? Author and TV host Scott Linden outlines some ways to encourage, motivate, and then help a new hunter on their first hunt.
From weather to shooting tips, to interacting with the dog, and what really counts on the hunt, Scott offers suggestions to ensure everyone has fun.
For more tips on hunting, dog training, and finding places to go: www.findbirdhuntingspots.com

programme.title: Identify your best prospect for a new hunter
programme.desc:
Picking the right new hunting partner is an art and a science ... and while there's no wrong way, some ways are righter than others. Author/TV host Scott Linden outlines some tips on finding the right person, how to set expectations, and what to tell them - and show them - before you make "the ask."
For more tips, go to www.findbirdhuntingspots.com

programme.title: The new-hunter best recruiter is your dog!
programme.desc:
Who doesn't love hunting dogs? The magic of their performance, excitement, and the adrenaline rush of a flush! One easy way to start a new hunter is to invite them to help train your dog.
Simple, short, convenient - there's no downside. And who wouldn't appreciate a little help with dog training?
Plus, some cool footage of a hunt with excellent dog works.
For more on starting a hunter, finding places to hunt, and dog training, go to www.findbirdhuntingspots.com.

programme.title: Ideas for finding new places to hunt
programme.desc:
Find upland birds on waterfowl production areas, and more tips on accessing public hunting areas are two of the topics ... as well as a great place to headquarter: Huron, South Dakota.
Watch some exciting bird hunting footage, too.
Find more information at www.findbirdhuntingspots.com

programme.title: Tailgate exam, part 2: wheels
programme.desc:
Part two covers your dog's "wheels," his feet. Enure a fantastic hunt tomorrow by keeping his feet healthy and injury-free with these step-by-step, toe-by-toe instructions.
Geet the entire exam in written form at HappyJackInc.com.

programme.title: Be nice, see where it gets you
programme.desc:
Walk-in hunting spots are not always easy to find. Here's an example of how to find them and the bonuses you might find along the way.
From hunting with a pro baseball player, to finding a black pheasant, to discovering new public-access spots in Huron, SD, there's a few lessons here.
Plus, some fun footage of a South Dakota pheasant hunt.
For more tips, go to www.findbirdhuntingspots.com

programme.title: Peak performance on Day Two: feed your dog strategically
programme.desc:
In the first 20 days of this season, my wirehair Flick had already hunted over 200 miles. He still scratches the RV door every morning, eager for another day of chukar chasing and quail quests.
I manage to keep up (mostly) with coffee and pain reliever. Flick, on the other paw, gets his stamina from Dr. Tim's dog food.
If your dog hunts multiple days in a row, it might be worth a look at how important food is to his performance. I asked Doctor Tim Hunt to share his thoughts on that, but first, a hunting story.

programme.title: Tailgate exam, Part 3: His steering wheel
programme.desc:
Okay, we've checked his body, his feet. But the tailgate exam isn't over until you've checked a dog's head – the steering wheel of your hunting machine. Like your truck, you're not getting very far without one! Put off that tall cold one for a couple more minutes. You'll have a fully-functioning hunting partner for the next day … and you won't die of thirst!
In this video, I'll show you where to look, what to look for and why ... and also how to remedy most common issues that might kibosh your next day's hunt, from getting stuff out of eyes and ears, to ensuring weeds and crud stay outta those places and more!
I'll take you step-by-step through all the deep, dark places that harbor danger and irritation on your dog's head so he's ready and rested for the next day's hunt.
And if you need remedies for any of the problems outlined, you can find them at www.happyjackinc.com.

programme.title: Get high, become a better bird hunter
programme.desc:
Not like that! I mean, boost your altitude - even just a bit - and you'll be able to keep a closer eye on your dog. If you're paying attention, you'll have a crucial half-second extra to get ready for a safe, sure shot.
I'll show you how - what you might use to get "up there" a little, what to look for in your dog's behavior, and why it's worth the effort.

programme.title: What's in my vest ... and why
programme.desc:
"Don't leave home without" is more than a cliche' from a TV commercial. What should you take on your next bird hunt, for you and your dog? Here's some advice on critical stuff, and what you might leave home ... without jeopardizing your safety or comfort - or you're dog's!
Somewhere in my personal vest is everything I need to shoot as well as possible (no smart remarks, please), stay found or get found, keep my dog safe and healthy, and help me survive a night or two in an emergency.
I'll show you all of it, and how to keep it from getting lost somewhere in the middle of nowhere!

programme.title: Your dog hurts - here's why
programme.desc:
I seem to be getting a lot of related questions since the season ended – most about aches and pains in our four-footed hunting buddies. And us!
The difference is, dogs won't show it like we do, with gripes and limping, complaints and wincing. They are way too loyal and hard working. It's why we love 'em.
You might already know this, but veterinarians tell me dogs seldom show pain. What they do, is slow down. Their pace in the field drags, they're slow to get out of their crate.
Maybe they won't jump onto your tailgate or training table.
That's probably arthritis, and it affects most dogs over eight years old. But here's the scary part: twenty percent of dogs show signs as early as one year old.
In this video, I'll show you how to prevent arthritis, manage it if your dog already has it, and what to avoid so he doesn't get it prematurely!

programme.title: Fuel your bird dog's peak performance ... but NOT with carbs!
programme.desc:
We hunt to watch our dogs work. So, stand by for plenty of that. But first, let me relate my last season. I tracked Flick's mileage. He averaged twenty-five miles a day, over almost fifty days in the field. I'm a lousy shooter, and okay trainer … so I'll attribute his stamina to my dumb luck, and his performance dog food.
If you want to watch your dog in the field day after day, heed some of the advice I got from Doctor Tim Hunt, a veterinarian, sled dog racer, and developer of the food Flick eats. He says the fuel you put in your dog directly impacts his ability to hunt hard, especially on a long hunting trip. He should know. His food has powered a bunch of Iditarod winners … and my guy Flick.
In this video, you'll learn what the key ingredients are in a dog food, how they work, and why. Hint: the most important component in your dog food is probably NOT what you think it is.

programme.title: Your bird dog's "suit of armor" and how it helps him reach his peak
programme.desc:
In previous videos, we've covered a dog's … headlights, wheels and steering wheel …
Now, it's time to cover a dog's largest organ, that I'll call his "body and paint," his skin and coat. Like a suit of armor, they protect a dog from virtually everything that can put him on the injured reserve list when he could be hunting.
To help you - and him - through a long season, I'll outline many of the problems that are easily handled without a vet visit, if you have a few things on hand, their potential causes, and what you can do about them so you both get back to hunting ASAP.
I'll also settle that proverbial campfire debate once and for all: are hair and fur are the same thing?

programme.title: Hunting dog peak performance on multi-day hunts
programme.desc:
There is a "magic dust" that can help your hunting dog's muscles recover overnight and keep him performing at his best on the second, third, and fourth days of a long hunting trip. The key is knowing what it is, how it works, and when to give it to him...and what NOT to give him at the same time!
I'll outline the how and why in this video ... plus some excellent dog work from Ruggs Ranch in Oregon just for fun!

programme.title: That ingredient sneaky dog food makers don't want you to know about
programme.desc:
Want less poop, and more dazzling performance from your hunting dog?
Generally, less poop means your dog food contains the highest-quality protein and his body is utilizing almost all of it.
But crafty dog food makers often hide the key ingredient ... the one that will tell ALL about the quality of the protein in your hunting dog's food. And it's the easiest way to tell how good your dog food is.
This ingredient is seldom on the label. You'll have to quit browsing puppy pictures on the Internet and go to the dog food maker's website. If you want more of his food fueling peak performance and less piling up in the yard, it's worth the effort.

programme.title: Four tips to get the most from your walk-in and public-access bird hunt
programme.desc:
So, you've picked out a public-access spot. The first thing you should do? Don't go there. You need a plan.
Here are four suggestions based on my trips to some of the hundreds of public access spots near Huron, South Dakota. I'll save you time, money and aggravation while helping you become a more productive bird hunter.
Your bird dog will thank you.

programme.title: 4 tips make your bird hunting road trip better ... for your dog
programme.desc: You'll both arrive at your bird hunting destination rested, relaxed, and ready for action with these four tips for hunting dog comfort and security.

programme.title: Go along to get along in bird hunting country
programme.desc:
Be a good temporary neighbor in hunting hotspots like Huron, South Dakota, and you'll reap benefits of all sorts. Here's a "field guide" to getting the most from your hunting destination.
Dial it down: Things move a bit more deliberately in rural America; we can too. Breathe deep at the gas station, tavern or sporting goods store. Fit in, and residents will welcome you … you'll have "a guy" in town.
Good guest: Let's give as good as we get: buy local, drive like locals, drink like locals. "Pay it forward," respect diverse values, and wire gates open more often.
It's their office: Cattle, crops, drilling, are part of the economic landscape. Empty shotgun shells can sideline a combine. Cows are walking thousand-dollar bills. An unattended campfire is like burning down someone's office.
The downside is obvious: locked gates, drive-by's while wrestling a flat tire. The payoff is also crystal clear: access, friends when you need them, useful information, textures and colors that make a hunting trip truly epic. Well, unless you shoot like me.
Free info pack: Access maps, Discounts, Prizes
I learned most of these lessons in the Ringneck Nation of Huron, South Dakota and so can you. Go to HuntHuronSD.com and request a free information pack and you're entered to win one of three hunting trip prize packages. See you there.

programme.title: Blood and guts! Simple field first aid for your dog.
programme.desc: When to race to the vet, and when you can do it yourself when a dog gets cut, scraped and scratched. Here are some simple tips to figure out what to do, how to do it, and why.

programme.title: A place for everything makes your bird hunting trips EPIC for you and your dog
programme.desc:
It's your big road trip of the season … and you've got a place for everything, and everything in its place. Right?
If you answered no, or maybe, or what? let's take those niggling details from forgotten to second nature for a trip that's more relaxed, productive, and fun … for both of you. In this case we're headed for Huron, South Dakota …
You may have your own system that works just fine, but maybe somewhere in here is something you hadn't thought of. I've learned most of this the hard way … so you don't have to. I forgot something, couldn't find it when I needed it, or inconvenience became emergency.
You'll also see some of the stuff I use to keep my dog healthy and at his peak on long hunts ... uncommon, unthought-of and definitely must-have if you want the best from your four-footed hunting buddy.

programme.title: The "Fearsome Four" ingredients that should never be in your dog's food
programme.desc:
Have you looked closely at your dog food label? There could be stuff in there that could cause allergy, seizures, even cancer. And it's in more dog foods than you think!
If you want to ensure your hunting dog's health and peak performance, learn what shouldn't be in dog food. Here's the list.
Oh, and enjoy some cool dog work from Horseshoe Curve hunt club in Oregon.

programme.title: Bird dog training: one (baby) step at a time

programme.desc: Your dog keys off your face as often as your verbal commands. If he can see your mug, he's more likely to follow some key commands.

programme.desc: Elect4ronic collars are great training aids, but there are times when you should keep the transmitter in your pocket. Here are some of them.

programme.title: Better bird dog retrieves: don't swipe it!
programme.desc: He worked hard to produce that bird, so what do you do the minute he brings it back? Swipe it! Here's why and how to do it right.

programme.title: Is your bird dog sensitive? The answer is yes.
programme.desc: Keep your hunting dog on an even keel by anticipating the stress-inducers and minimizing their effect. YOu'll get better performance.

programme.title: Four tips to public access bird hunting
programme.desc: Before you go hunting, STOP. Lay a plan. Scott offers four tips to get you to more public access bird hunting.

programme.title: Bird hunting ROAD TRIP! Make the drive better for your hunting dog
programme.desc: Your dog needs to arrive fresh, safe, and rested. Scott outlines four ways to ensure he's at his peak when you drop the tailgate on that long-distance hunting destination.

programme.title: Bird hunting: get along by going along and you'll get the most from any hunting destination
programme.desc: Adjust your pace, check your ego at the county line, and you'll have "a guy" in town. Scott offers tips on how being a good visitor might open a gate or two for the best public-access hunting.

programme.title: A place for everything on your bird hunting road trip
programme.desc: Pack your rig for efficiency, dog health, and productivity. You'll be ready for most situations, able to find and access public ground, and your dog will be happier too.

programme.title: Be nice, and skunkwise, with a steady dog
programme.desc:
A chance encounter on the road leads to an invitation to hunt ... that's the good news. That in turn led to new friendships and (luckily) some solid dog work. The worst-case could have put a real damper on the day.
Some advice on accessing walk-in ground, and footage of excellent dogs working wild birds are also included in this short lesson in common courtesy and its rewards.

programme.title: Finding public access bird hunting ground ... here's how
programme.desc: Here are a number of tips and tactics on finding walk-in hunting land in South Dakota, including lesser-known and uncrowded spots most people drive past. Today, we focus on the how and why ... from digital mapping to where to go on those free hunting spots. Hunting strategies are also covered, as well as what bird species hang out where.

programme.title: Coachella ... for bird dog guys!
programme.desc: Here's an event that showcases you and your dog's skills, whatever your experience level. While we enjoy great dog work, learn more about safe shooting, and hunting strategies.

programme.title: Want worms? Take your dog hunting.
programme.desc:
Your dog picks up worms every time his feet hit the ground. You touch them, or he licks you, and you've got them too.
Here are smart, simple ways to deal with the most common worms, and why it's important if you want him - and you - to perform at your peak.

programme.title: Public access bird hunting: have a plan
programme.desc: Here are four tips to get you into free bird hunting spots. Digital scouting, alternate access points, use all available resources from game departments to hotel clerks, scouting tips to save time and aggravation, and how to hunt once you get there to stay away from the crowd ... if there is one.

programme.title: DESTINATION: bird hunting somewhere in South Dakota
programme.desc:
First in a series on places to hunt wild birds on public land ... from over 30 years traveling 26 states in pursuit of wild birds.
Why? Hunters are the first - and biggest - force in conservation. Our gun, ammo, bow and arrow purchases fund virtually all habitat and wildlife management. If hunting is to survive so your grandchildren can experience the magic we do, or if we're to keep people hunting, we've got to help them find new places to hunt ... so they'll continue to buy guns and ammo.
Don't get your undies in a wad. I won't share any place that's not already "discovered," or your secret spot, but I will share places that can stand a little more pressure. Never will there be a lat/long or specific honey holes ... you gotta earn them! But here's your starting point.
And if you want more, go to https://findbirdhuntingspots.com
Let me know what you think. Scott

programme.title: Three tips to better bird hunting ... get your head in the game
programme.desc:
Simple is better, especially when it comes to shooting birds flushing all around you. Here are three bird hunting tips that will help you connect more often and make your dog even happier.
It starts with your head, literally.
Made possible by LegacySports.com/pointer

programme.title: Bird hunting, after the point: these tips make all the difference between "fetch" and "*$^%$(^*^!"
programme.desc:
Once your dog stands the bird, the rest is up to you. What you do and how you do it is the difference between "fetch" and "&*%##@(!"
Here are some tips on approaching the dog and the bird, foot placement and more.
See more videos and tips at https://legacysports.com/pointer

programme.title: Bird hunters: shoot like a predator, make your dog happy
programme.desc:
Focus. Yep, not just on the flying bird, but on the beak. You've got enough distractions, from a dog on point to the beautiful scenery to your judgmental hunting buddy.
Here, I'll show you how to achieve a laser-like vision that ultimately puts more birds on the ground. And that's what your dog wants, isn't it?

programme.title: Bird dog emergency ... or not? Here's how to tell the difference.
programme.desc:
It's a jungle out there. And a desert, stubble field, swamp, and popple thicket. Yuk. Every one of those hunting scenarios can cut, scratch, sting, bite or infect your dog. And each needs your attention if you hope to finish the day … or the season.
I'll outline the serious stuff that if your human hunting partner had one of these problems, you'd go to the emergency room. For the other stuff, over-the-counter and D-I-Y solutions may be all you need. If you have them handy, the day or the season are saved. I'll show you the stuff I've got ready in my truck.

programme.title: Better bird hunting with a better shot pattern
programme.desc:
In the days of silk fly lines, English fly anglers would utter "God save the queen," before setting the hook. This gave the trout time to take the fly in his mouth and turn, setting the hook himself rather than the angler pulling it away too soon.
I'm convinced it's good advice for bird hunters too, for a slightly different reason.
Here are two easy ways to put the odds in your favor … and keep your bird dog happy.

programme.title: All in one piece: the complete tailgate exam keeps your bird dog safe and healthy after every hunt
programme.desc: Do this first ... after every hunt. You'll enjoy a long and productive bird season thanks to a healthy, happy dog. I'll give you step-by-step instructions on what to look for and how.

programme.title: Will your dog shoot someone this season?
programme.desc:
In the heat of the hunt, safety goes out the window sometimes. Here are some key moments when firearms, dogs, and humans don't always play well together.
Here are the goofs that are easiest to forget when feathers fly and dogs, well, act like dogs.

programme.title: Bird dog training: One step at a time
programme.desc:
A dog doesn't just "get it." He needs to learn every skill in increments ... bits and pieces that eventually add up to a flawless retrieve, steady point, or simply to come when called. Here are tips to ensure you start right, and end with a polished performance.
More tips: findbirdhuntingspots.com

programme.title: Bird dog training: your face helps, no matter how ugly you are!
programme.desc: Like me, you might have a "face for radio," but your dog doesn't mind. He looks to you, literally, for direction. Here's how it works, why, and how to use it to your advantage in the yard and in the field.

programme.title: Get your bird dog back ... let him savor that retrieve
programme.desc:
Dogs naturally want to take a shot bird and bury it, or eat it, or at least keep it away from you. But if you aren't grabbing it the moment he arrives, he may be a bit more willing to "share."
Here are tips on how to make your dog a better retriever brought to you by www.findbirdhuntingspots.com, your source for dog training and public-access hunting information.

programme.title: Bird dog basics: when to keep your e-collar out of the transaction
programme.desc: There are times when the best thing to do with an electronic training collar is nothing. I'll show you when and why to avoid using this helpful training tool.

programme.title: Your bird dog is more sensitive than you think
programme.desc: Introduce your dog gradually to new sounds, people, habitat types and he'll become a better hunter. How? open your own eyes, ears and nose.

programme.title: Honest is the best policy with your hunting dog
programme.desc: Tell the truth, so to speak, when training your bird dog. He'll trust you more, learn faster, and both of you will be closer to peak performance. Here are some common mistakes we make that might be fun or funny to us, but booger up your dog training.

programme.title: Get high while bird hunting!
programme.desc: Not that. Nope. I mean boosting your elevation in the field. You'll see your dog when he starts getting birdy. That, in turn, leads to better shooting for you.

programme.desc:
From my new webinar, here are two of the 107 tips that will help you find better publicly-accessible bird hunting ground. Want them all? Start here:
https://www.bigmarker.com/linden-media/Public-access-adventures-A-bird-hunter-s-plan-based-on-32-years-and-26-states-of-wild-bird-hunting-in-publicly-accessible-land

programme.title: Better shooting means happier bird dogs
programme.desc: The key to bird-dog happines is birds on the ground for him to retrieve. That mean you need to up your shooting game. Here are tips on doing that, from how you wear your hat, to where you put your feet.

programme.title: Bird dog habits: break 'em
programme.desc: You're creating a creature of habit and it's not a good thing. Here's how to interrupt the chain that leads to complacency or disobedience.

programme.title: Your hunting dog is a sensitive guy - help him "get over it"
programme.desc: Stress affects your bird dog's performance. Here are tips on lightening the impact from surroundings, sounds, people and places.

programme.title: When your hunting dog won't retrieve
programme.desc: Tips and hacks to help your dog bring that bird back after you shoot it ... starting with don't take it!

programme.title: Ready to shoot that bird? Probably not!
programme.desc: It looks easy, until you try it. You're probably doing one or more things wrong when you shoot at flushing birds. Here is one simple way to ensure your gun moves where the bird goes ... and so do your eyes, head, hands, and shot string!

programme.title: Dance with your dog for more birds
programme.desc: The way you move around your dog once he's pointed can be the difference between a hit and a miss. There are other benefits, too. Here's what I mean.

programme.title: Shoot the first one, first
programme.desc: Trying to drop a double? You'll miss, if you shoot like me. Here are some suggestions that might improve your chances.

programme.title: Shhhh! It's the key to better bird hunting
programme.desc: Zip your lips, quiet your dog, silence your gear. Shoot more birds. Here are some suggestions.

programme.title: Don't be a greedy bird dog owner
programme.desc: Hey showoff: you're ruining your dog when you run him through too many reps just to get your friends jealous. Here are some suggestions that keep him fresh and responsive.

programme.title: The real reason a bird dog won't retrieve ... sometimes
programme.desc: It's not about disobedience, sometimes. There's a more fundamental reason your bird dog won't bring back what you just shot. Here's why you should cut him some slack.

programme.title: Tips & tricks for better bird hunting
programme.desc: Even a "face for radio" won't stop your dog from following direction ... and might help. Plus a webinar excerpt on finding more public access lands, shoot better with these two tips, and get better retrieves by letting your hunting dog keep the bird for a while.

programme.title: Upland school: teach an old dog new tricks, shooting better, and more
programme.desc: A series of video tips: teach an old dog, getting ready to shoot, coping with dog training setbacks and more.

programme.title: Bird huners: train your dog, shoot better and hunt more strategically
programme.desc: This mixed bag of tips and tactics will make you a better hunter and keep your bird dog happy!

programme.title: Upland Nation University: bird hunting tips and tactics
programme.desc: From dog training to shooting better, here is advice that will help you become a better bird hunter.

programme.title: Upland Nation University: bird hunting tips and tactics, Vol. 3
programme.desc: Tips, tactics, advice and insights that will help you become a better dog trainer, bird hunter and wingshooter. You might even find more public-access and walk-in hunting ground! Your dog will thank you.

programme.title: Four tips to better bird hunting
programme.desc: Dog training, shooting and strategy from America's favorite TV host.

programme.title: Better bird hunting: tips and tricks
programme.desc: Eleven minutes of tips and tricks for you and your bird dog

programme.title: Upland Nation University
programme.desc: A continuing series to help you become a better bird hunter, dog trainer and wingsohoter.

programme.title: Highlight reel: Southern Illinois mixed bag
programme.desc: Our first of two visits to big whitetail country ... for upland birds. A ton of dogs and hard-flying birds, some incredible dog work and okay shooting. Training tips, game cooking advice and a showcase of a rare Italian breed.

programme.title: Highlight reel: Southern Illinois mixed bag, part 2
programme.desc: Return to Illinois, where we chase wily ringnecks and bobwhites among a variety of habitats with young and old dogs. Hunting tips, dog training advice and more.

programme.title: Oh say can you see ... your muzzle?
programme.desc:
Have you ever thought about how your mind works when you shoot a shotgun? "Aiming," versus pointing, "swing through" or some other style, foot position, one eye or two? No matter your preference, your head needs to "see" the shotgun muzzle, right? Not overtly, but subconciously.
Here's a video that might help explain it. Maybe. You decide, and see if there's something there to help. Made possible by HiVizSights.com.

programme.title: Upland Nation University: bird hunting tips and tactics
programme.desc: From the first part of a "tailgate exam" for your dog, to getting (more) ready to shoot, here is a short course in dog handling and bird hunting.

programme.title: Upland Nation University Part 4
programme.desc: Tips and tactics for bird hunters and dog trainers, this week including the full tailgate exam, shooting straighter with a different stance, and a dog training tactic you may not have thought about.

programme.title: See the bird by not seeing it
programme.desc: Training your eyes - and head - to see the bird or clay target in the right way at the right time is critical to hitting it. It's a simple, but critical process starting with unfocused eyes, then zooming in, laser-like, on the target. Here's how.

programme.title: Snow? Go inside and slow down to bag more birds
programme.desc: Even in crappy weather, you can practice your shotgunning ... indoors. But most of us rush many aspects of the move-mount-shoot process and never quite get dialed into the target as a result. Try this simple drill and maybe you'll hit a few more birds or clay targets.

programme.title: Slow down for more birds
programme.desc:
You set the pace in the field, and if you're in a rush so is your dog. That means less time in a scent cone and more missed birds.
Scott Linden of Wingshooting USA TV shows you how, and explains why, you should dial things down a bit when it comes to covering a field or covert.
If you want more tips on dog training and bird hunting, go to: www.findbirdhuntingspots.com

programme.title: Get high, become a better bird hunter
programme.desc:
Not like that! I mean, boost your altitude - even just a bit - and you'll be able to keep a closer eye on your dog. If you're paying attention, you'll have a crucial half-second extra to get ready for a safe, sure shot.
I'll show you how - what you might use to get "up there" a little, what to look for in your dog's behavior, and why it's worth the effort.

programme.title: Bird hunters: shoot like a predator, make your dog happy
programme.desc:
Focus. Yep, not just on the flying bird, but on the beak. You've got enough distractions, from a dog on point to the beautiful scenery to your judgmental hunting buddy.
Here, I'll show you how to achieve a laser-like vision that ultimately puts more birds on the ground. And that's what your dog wants, isn't it?

programme.title: Bulls, Bucks, & Beards!
programme.desc: Crafting the ultimate outdoor experience is Rick Taylor's cup of tea. Rick is a lifetime outdoorsman and currently works for BPI Outdoors as their Social Media Strategist. In this episode, he shares his passion for hunting, guiding and just being outdoors. He has had the opportunity to guide elk hunts in Tennessee, pass his love of hunting to his kids, and help his dad harvest his first buck later in life. This is a must-watch if you love hunting. Don't miss it!

programme.desc: Charles puts the latest gear from Dead Air Silencers to the test in this action-packed episode. Meanwhile, the team makes a veteran's dream come true by taking him on a bucket-list helicopter hunt for hogs, delivering an unforgettable experience.

programme.desc: Firefighters black bear hunting in Canada.

programme.title: Serber's Bear
programme.desc: Canada bear hunt with a bow in the snow and cold temps.

programme.title: Bow Hunting Osceola Gobblers

programme.title: Noah and His Nature
programme.desc: As with most great hunting stories, this one holds infinite meaning as Host Phillip Vanderpool and 16 year old Noah Walters share the turkey woods through the 2015 Kidz Outdoors event. Phillip guides Noah through the hunt, while Noah shares his nature of love and passion with everyone involved.

programme.title: Conquering Your Fears
programme.desc: Norissa doubts herself after missing a shot on an excellent trophy, but recovers her confidence soon after and learns not to judge herself too harshly. PH Marius patiently guides them and helps them build their hunting career and confidence as huntresses. Norissa has to conquer her fear of heights in this episode as Jen tries to convince her to take a leap of faith, by jumping out of an airplane.

programme.title: First Experiences In Africa
programme.desc: After a whirlwind two weeks, Jen and Norissa find themselves in Africa. Not knowing the culture, the animals or their new producer Kappie. Their journey starts with learning how to track these majestic animals in Africa, and Norissa finds herself being pushed out of her comfort zone on the first trip. Follow their journey from the start and see how they grow into experienced and talented huntresses.

programme.title: New Zealand Treasures
programme.desc: Jen and Norissa are heading to New Zealand this week to look for a Thar and a Chamois with their friends from Doddsy's Hunting Experience. Stalking in the open fields and having to take long distance shots are just some of the challenges they'll have to overcome. Norissa will have to push herself to adapt to the ever-changing circumstances that comes with this difficult hunt, and face her fear of heights as Jen tries to convince her to bungee jump off the highest bridge in New Zealand.

programme.title: Northern Cape Surprises
programme.desc: Jen and Norissa travel to the Northern Cape of South Africa to hunt with Wintershoek Safaris. The hunt starts with a laugh as Jen realizes yet again how short she is, especially in comparison to their PH Yvan. This new terrain is challenging and comes with many obstacles during their hunt for a Black Wildebeest and Red Hartebeest. Adrenaline runs high, as Jen has to change tactics in a matter of seconds to get her trophy and Norissa gets a pleasant surprise when lining up to shoot her trophy. The team also journeys to Kimberley Hole, the famous diamond mine in South Africa.

programme.title: Freezing Africa, But Warm Friendships
programme.desc: Jen and Norissa are back at Wintershoek Safaris, in the Northern Cape of South Africa this week. In this episode they are in pursuit of a Gemsbuck and a Springbuck. PH Yvan discovers the ups and downs from hunting with two female hunters and his adrenaline is high as Jen gets in place to take aim on a trophy. They learn a lot of this new area and get to see nature's way of making silk. There is a wounded Buffalo in the area and the team is on high alert as they're very cautious of every noise and movement while tracking one of Norissa's favorite animals, a Gemsbuck. A lot of excitement and adrenalin in this episode!

programme.title: Limitless
programme.desc: This week Jen and Norissa are back in New Zealand hunting with Doddsy's Hunting Experience. Not having to sit in the office back in CA, is a welcome change for Jen and Norissa as they enjoy the outdoors and physical challenges of this trip. Emotions run high as Norissa tries to take a long distance shot in an uncomfortable position and Jen discovers that harvesting her Chamois trophy might just be half the challenge in this audacious country.

programme.title: The White Mountain
programme.desc: This week Jen and Norissa travel to the Freestate hunting with Witkop Safaris. Their PH and Outfitter Jess de Klerk will be guiding them along with good friend and guest Morgan Mills. Norissa is in persuit of an Eland, but will the big open plains and too many eyes allow her to get into shooting distance. Morgan experiences the value of a one-shot-kill in this action pack episode. Morgan also ventures down an African river-rafting experience.

programme.title: Facing One Of The Dangerous 7
programme.desc: This week Jen and Norissa, along with guest Morgan Mills travel to Zimbabwe, where they will be hunting with Martin Pieters Safaris. Their PH for this trip, Bruce, has his hands full with their first female hunters in camp. Long, hot days and challenging stalks lead to Jen gearing up to take the first of her African Dangerous 7 animals.

programme.title: Scarecrow Stalking
programme.desc: This week Jen and Norissa are back at Wintershoek Safaris, in the Northern Cape of South Africa. Jen is in search of a Springbuck trophy and they visit the Wild Hearts Rehab center. They play with a baby Rhino at the rehab center and Jen almost gets her sunglasses stolen by a monkey. Jen and Norissa learns about tracking animals in Africa and how walking and stalking in these terrains can be very different and amusing.

programme.title: One-Eye Gemsbuck
programme.desc: Jen and Norissa travel to Namibia this week to hunt with Agagia Safaris. They will be hunting in the semi-desert area of South West Africa looking for a Gemsbuck. After an eventful stalk they soon realize it could have been a lot easier. This is a fun week with the team out playing on the sand dunes with ATV's and snowboards. Don't miss this fun and exciting episode.

programme.title: Challenging The Outfitter
programme.desc: Jen and Norissa are still in Namibia with Agagia Safaris this week. After becoming good friends with outfitter and PH Carin Neetling, they challenge her to a hunt; she accepts the challenge and joins Jen and Norissa in pursuit of a Zebra. Later Jen and Norissa experience sea life with an unexpected visit.

programme.title: Darting A Rhino
programme.desc: Jen and Norissa are back at Wintershoek Safaris, this week they will be darting a White Rhino. Due to Rhino pouching green hunts on Rhinos are illegal in South Africa, vita dart safaris are the new green hunt on rhinos, never done before in the Northern Cape of South Africa, Norissa becomes the pioneer for the first vita dart safari in this province. This episode we will talk to the authorities and find out how Rhino vita darting can still generate an income and by doing so help save the Rhino species.

programme.title: Where To Next?
programme.desc: Jen, Norissa and producer Kappie flashback on the adventures they've had so far, how much they've grown and all the highs and lows of their journey so far.

programme.title: Bongo In The Congo pt. 1
programme.desc: The trip begins with last minute changes and unforeseen challenges. From driving through the forest for 25 hours, to 13 hour hunting days, see if Norissa gets her Bongo trophy after an exhausting week.

programme.title: Bongo In The Congo pt. 2
programme.desc: In the previous episode Norissa got her Bongo trophy and now it's Jen's turn. Time is running out, with only 2 days of hunting left, and Jen is feeling the pressure, and the long days are beginning to show its toll on the whole team. Will she get her trophy in time?

programme.title: The Fast And The Furious
programme.desc: Jen, Norissa and guest host Morgan Mills travel to South Africa to hunt at Witkop Safaris, with Outfitter and PH Jess De Klerk.

The team also has a good laugh taking a tango lesson in Buenos Aires, embracing everything this adventurous country has to offer.

programme.title: The Argentina Gaucho
programme.desc: Jen is in pursuit of a Red Stag, and Norissa has a surprisingly good morning hunting for her blackbuck.Jen, Norissa and Kappie will also be joining the TGB team in a traditional day rounding up the cattle. Jen reminisces in her memories of her rodeo days, Norissa can't wait to share this with her father in-law and Kappie tries to balance horse and camera.

programme.title: Those Who Hunt Together, Stay Together pt. 1

programme.title: Texas Red Sheep

programme.title: Those Who Hunt Together, Stay Together pt. 2
programme.desc: Norissa and Brian are still looking for a Cape Buffalo. Jen and Jon are enjoying each others company in the blind, observing some oversize visitors at the waterhole. On this episode Jen and Jon makes it official at an intimate wedding in Red Bluff, California. Join the team for an episode that shows the bonds between friendship and love, and how sharing in experience can strengthen any relationship.

programme.desc: Jen and Norissa travel to Pennsylvania for a Whitetail hunt with Quest Haven Outfitters. Patience is a virtue on this hunt. Also, join her on a special hunt where she takes her niece on her first turkey hunt. Teaching the next generation the importance of conservation and hunting is one of Jen's passions.

programme.desc: Jen and Norissa reflect back to their time in the Congo while speaking to Jerry at Safari Club International. programme.title: A Turkey Hunt Goes South in the Florida Swamp
programme.desc:
Welcome to Season 1, Episode 3 of Seek and Find TV! This episode is all about chasing a turkey through a Florida swamp! Reese and Amber decided to let Scott, guide them through their home turf (aka the swamp) since he's the expert turkey caller, and what happened was a disaster! He found the turkey.... but he also found out how quick things can go south in the swamp! This turkey hunting episode will for sure have you laughing and keep you excited the whole time!
Seek and Find TV was founded by Scott Hinnant of Conviction Outdoors and Reese Richards of Bearded Outdoors. The two friends came together and decided to create an outdoor show with a twist of Jesus. They equally share a love and passion for all things hunting, fishing, and anything in the outdoors, but what really brought these two together is their love for Jesus and passion to spread His name. Scott resides in Mississippi and Reese in Florida, so the episodes for Seek and Find TV will have a good variety of scenery and things to do in the outdoors.
Please let us know if you enjoy watching our episodes and if there is anything specific you'd like us to create. Please be sure to subscribe as well. God Bless!

programme.title: First Osceola Turkey on Florida Public Land
programme.desc:
Welcome to Season 1, Episode 2 of Seek and Find TV! This episode is all about turkey hunting! Scott and Reese wanted to bless Amber with her first turkey so they took her out on some Florida public land. Amber ended up being late for the turkey hunt but still ended up shooting her first turkey! A public land Osceola Turkey at that! Let us know what your favorite part is in the comments!
Seek and Find TV was founded by Scott Hinnant of Conviction Outdoors and Reese Richards of Bearded Outdoors. The two friends came together and decided to create an outdoor show with a twist of Jesus. They equally share a love and passion for all things hunting, fishing, and anything in the outdoors, but what really brought these two together is their love for Jesus and passion to spread His name. Scott resides in Mississippi and Reese in Florida, so the episodes for Seek and Find TV will have a good variety of scenery and things to do in the outdoors.
Please let us know if you enjoy watching our episodes and if there is anything specific you'd like us to create. Please be sure to subscribe as well. God Bless!

programme.title: Not Another Black Movie
programme.desc:
Not Another Black Movie stars Damon Williams (Bad Boys of Comedy, Comic View, BET LIVE, The Tom Joyner Morning Show), Janet Hubert (The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air), Rodney Perry (The Monique Show, Who's Got Jokes) Jay Davis (Not Another Zombie Movie, Shots Fired), and Leon Rogers (WGCI, Comic View, Bad Boys of Comedy).
Not Another Black Movie is not only a spoof of a genre often associated with Tyler Perry films, but a satirical look at family dysfunction as well. Written by Jay Davis and Directed by Donte "Diesel" Williams, Not Another Black Movie addresses issues that effect many families whether they be rich or poor, black or white. Although we poke fun at some of the stereotypical roles portrayed in this genre, we hope to shed some light on problems that plague many families while giving you a good laugh.

programme.title: BEONDTV is a Los Angeles-based broadcast and digital media network with a wide variety of original programming curated by Emmy award-winning journalists and content creators.
BEONDTV is a Los Angeles-based broadcast and digital media network with a wide variety of original programming curated by Emmy award-winning journalists and content creators.
Dropped - S02:E05 - Saddle Sores
programme.desc: The guys are feeling great as they leave sheep territory, but the 22-hour trip to Tom-Tom, the first moose camp, feels endless. It'll take them two long days of riding to get there. As they head into moose land with a successful sheep packed up high, trouble always seems just around the corner on their journey. After riding for eight hours, issues start cropping up.

programme.title: Miracles of Nature - S01:E04 - Naturally Exotic
programme.desc: This Episode of Miracles of Nature takes you on a journey from the Antigua in the Caribbean to the favourite of climbers - the Blue Mountains of New South Wales, Australia and then back to the Caribbean to admore in the beauty of The British Virgin Islands with stunning white beaches and turquoise waters.

programme.title: Miracles of Nature - S01:E05 - Naturally Fierce
programme.desc: Visit the wintry North Pole from the comfort of your settee as this episode takes us on a journey to the icy Artic and then to Quebec to watch the most southernly fjord set at low tide, before journeying on to Alberta to take in the magnitude of the Sasquachuan River as it makes its way through the Rocky Mountains.

programme.title: The Luxury Travel Show - S01:E07 - Uga Bay, Sri Lanka and Istanbul
programme.desc: The Luxury Travel Show heads to the idyllic resort of Uga Beach in Sri Lanka for some unusual fine dining locations, with tall tables in the swimming pool and dug-out sunken tables in the sand. Then it’s off to Istanbul with a stay in one of the city’s best hotels - which has been transformed from a derelict tobacco factory into a palace fit for royalty.

programme.title: Diana: In Search of Happiness
programme.desc: Experience an in-depth look at Princess Diana, the extraordinary woman of the 20th century. Featuring unique interviews and touching clips, this portrait captures her incredible journey to fame and her ability to overcome the emotional and physical challenges she encountered nearly every day.

programme.title: Royal Documentaries - S01:E28 - Diana And Sarah The Royal Wives Of Windsor Part 2
programme.desc: Diana, Princess of Wales, and Sarah, Duchess of York both married into the Queen's family, leaving in the midst of scandals, though their exits were quite different. Sadly, Diana passed away, while Sarah survived to start anew. Over time, their struggles can be better understood, and this documentary explores those challenges...

programme.title: Wardens - S02:E04 - Operation Snow Cat
programme.desc: Montana Game Wardens ride snowmobiles through the mountains in winter. It's elk hunting season, so they also make sure everyone is following the hunting rules.

programme.title: Dropped - S02:E06 - Church on the Mountain
programme.desc: In the Yukon, decisions can change everything in a heartbeat, especially in such a tough landscape. The brothers are closing in on the enormous mountain grizzly, now just 500 yards away, and it's up to Chris to make the call.

programme.title: Miracles of Nature - S01:E06 - Naturally Forged
programme.desc: In this episode of Miracles of Nature visits several different islands. Expect to see the breathtaking terrace rocks of Taiwan and the majestic volcano on the mythic island of Bali. On to the island of Jersey, after which a part of New York is named, and finally we visit the spectacular Madeira, which features an amazing variety of landscapes despite being a few kilometres in length.

programme.title: Miracles of Nature - S01:E07 - Naturally Majestic
programme.desc: Follow in the footsteps of Indiana Jones. In this episode of Miracles of Nature we visit the wonders of the Gobi Desert which is one of the oldest deserts in the world, and then the contrasting lush, green hillsides of northern Mongolian. From there we travel 5000 kilometres to the south east to Jordan and the Dead Sea.

programme.title: The Luxury Travel Show - S01:E09 - Rennes and Provo
programme.desc: This gastronomic tour of Brittany stops off for crêpes in Rennes and Oysters in Cancale before visiting the historic walled city of St Malo. Then on to the island of Providenciales, known locally as Provo, in the Turks and Caicos Caribbean islands with buggy racing on the beach and a spot of shopping for some very expensive wines.

programme.title: The Luxury Travel Show - S01:E10 - Stockholm and Lisbon
programme.desc: For a weekend winter break, Stockholm has got to be one of most beautiful cities to visit. Made up of 14 separate islands, it’s one of the best-preserved and largest mediaeval cities in Europe. Then some summer sun in the Portuguese capitol, Lisbon, for a whistle stop cultural tour of the city and a surfing lesson along the coast.

programme.title: Jim Shockey's Uncharted - S01:E10 - The Ancient Ones
programme.desc: Arctic. Jim and Corey's Arctic adventure starts with Muskox, an animal practically forgotten since pre-historic times in the Arctic.

programme.title: Royal Documentaries - S01:E32 - Prince William Royal Teenage Behind The Scenes
programme.desc: Who's the real person beneath all those glamorous royal photos? This intriguing documentary takes a look into the life of the young man behind the public image.

programme.title: Wardens - S02:E05 - Operation Litter Bug
programme.desc: Working to protect our treasured natural resources in some of the country's most secluded spots means there's never a boring day on the job.

programme.title: Dropped - S02:E07 - Valley of Snow
programme.desc: The Keefer brothers are stuck at Church Camp as the snow keeps pounding down, and they can barely see anything. They're snowed in and don't know when they'll be able to continue their hunting trip. They're starting to face a bunch of problems.

programme.title: Miracles of Nature - S01:E08 - Naturally Raw
programme.desc: This episode begins in Costa Rica, in an amazing rain forest. Here they make delicious chocolate out of cocoa beans. Mother Nature is at her magnificent best – showcasing hundreds of plant and animal species. And then to Kenya where green monkeys will be our tour-guides in the Lost City of Gedi plus a closer look at the wildlife which lives in very close proximity to the bustling streets of Nairobi.

programme.title: Miracles of Nature - S01:E09 - Naturally Invigorating
programme.desc: Iceland: home to volcanic lakes and hot springs and mono-chromatic vistas. And then to Laos in South East Asia with its lush jungles, underground caves and water buffalo along the Mekong River.

programme.title: The Luxury Travel Show - S01:E11 - The Loire and Grenada
programme.desc: There’s more to the Loire Valley in France than wine. We’re on the Da Vinci trail, following in the last footsteps and final resting place of the great Leonardo da Vinci in the small town of Amboise, deep in the heart of the Loire. Then for the ultimate in relaxation it’s a pamper and spa break in Grenada.

programme.title: The Luxury Travel Show - S01:E12 - Venice and Northern Ireland
programme.desc: Venice, one of Europe’s most iconic and enchanting cities with its labyrinth of waterways and canals linking one hundred and eighteen separate islands. From Venetians to visitors, it’s the city where everyone oozes style. Then on to Northern Ireland, for a ghostly trail around a haunted hotel and a walk on the road to Winterfel, visiting some of the iconic locations featured HBO’s Games of Thrones series.

programme.title: Jim Shockey's Uncharted - S01:E11 - True North
programme.desc: Arctic Pt2. Inuit Elders provide guidance as Jim and Corey prepare to face the ice once again on a special invite to document a traditional Inuit hunting expedition.

programme.title: Royal Documentaries - S01:E34 - Prince William And Prince Harry The Next Royal Generation
programme.desc: Prince William and Prince Harry, along with their friends, got as much media attention as today’s pop stars, fashion icons, and movie celebs. This documentary explores how this affected their personal lives and friendships, showcasing how they managed their fame alongside their royal responsibilities.

programme.title: Carter's W.A.R. - S02:E05 - Capturing the Wild
programme.desc: After seeing the disappearance of wildlife in northern Africa, Ivan joins an elite capture team to see how wildlife is captured, bought, and sold. This 'Wildlife Trade' is a ground breaking business model that could change the entire face of conservation in Africa.

programme.title: Wild Ones - S01:E09 - Disguised
programme.desc: Now you see me… now you don’t. A look at the masters of disguise. From hidden lizards and invisible spiders to camouflaged cats and shimmering squids.

programme.title: Wild Ones - S01:E10 - Micro Predators
programme.desc: They may be small but don’t be fooled - micro predators can be deadly. From the impressive serial killer Portia spider to the hundreds of species of ants and the archerfish with its precision firing of water droplets to secure its prey Wild Ones peers through the microscope to uncover their true lethality.

programme.title: Wild Ones - S01:E11 - Most Poisonous_
programme.desc: You wouldn’t want to be bitten by any of these but which one has the deadliest poison? The venom from the most poisonous snake on the planet? A rare poisonous lizard? Or is it the blue ringed octopus?

programme.title: Wild Ones - S01:E12 - Migration
programme.desc: Animals, big and not so big, traverse hundreds of miles – some in search of food, others to find ideal breeding grounds. From Zebras crossing the savannahs of Africa to the huge journeys undertaken by turtles to find the perfect beach to lay their eggs – the annual and often dangerous journeys are simply mind boggling.

programme.title: Miracles of Nature - S02:E06 - Naturally Miraculous
programme.desc: In the rain forests of the Seychelles we encounter remarkable fauna and flora. Then on to Mauritius. Where the symbol of the cruel and inconsiderate colonization of Africa is the extinct Dodo bird. We conclude today’s episode in the very heart of Africa, in the only place on the planet where close relatives to humans, the mountain gorillas - live. The country is the Democratic Republic of Congo and the province we shall visit is South Kivu.

programme.title: Miracles of Nature - S02:E07 - Naturally Fascinating
programme.desc: Bolivia is a country of countless fascinating natural sights. We will begin on the high plateau of Altiplano, stopping by the world’s largest salt lake.Later, we will descend a few thousand meters using the road of death to the Los Yungas province. And then on to the shores of lake Titicaca, the highest navigable lake in the world.

programme.title: Miracles of Nature - S02:E08 - Naturally Harmonious
programme.desc: Zambia, the Latvian region of Kurzeme, the Georgian provinces of Kakheti and Svaneti, seem to have very little in common. They lie in Africa, Europe and on the borderline between Europe and Asia respectively. Kakheti and Svaneti are both a part of Georgia but very unlike one another. So where is the connection? How are these regions similar?

programme.title: Miracles of Nature - S02:E09 - Naturally Spiritual
programme.desc: In this episode we visit two different corners of our planet. Although thousands of kilometres apart, spiritually they are close relatives. First, Ethiopia in East Africa which is dissected by the Great African Rift Valley and considered by many to be the cradle of humankind. Next, a paradise on Earth: Jamaica.

programme.title: Sasquatch Mountain Man - S05:E01 - Mule Deer
programme.desc: Laramy rides the high lonesome in search of a mountain mule deer. Learn the old mountain man techniques to stalk in close to a big mule deer buck.

programme.title: Sasquatch Mountain Man - S05:E02 - Alaska Caribou Part 1
programme.desc: Deep in the Alaskan territory, Laramy hunts the frontier in search of caribou. When a hungry grizzly sniffs around camp, will Laramy's single shot rifle be enough protection?

programme.title: Sasquatch Mountain Man - S05:E03 - Montana Mountain Lion
programme.desc: Laramy lets loose the dogs and rides the snowy mountains in search of the big game cat of North America, the mountain lion.

programme.title: Sasquatch Mountain Man - S05:E04 - Trapping Part 1
programme.desc: Springtime begins as Laramy honors the history of the mountain men by trapping for beaver and other critters.

programme.title: 10 Inch Hero
programme.desc: An artist gets a job at a beachside sandwich shop, where she hangs out with a techie, a flirt, a rocker, a hippie, and a Wiccan.

programme.title: Alien Trespass
programme.desc: After crash landing on the outskirts of a desert town, an alien enlists the help of a local waitress to recapture a monster that has escaped the wreckage of his spaceship in this affectionate, knowing, hilarious send-up of a genreís sillier past.

programme.title: Eavesdrop
programme.desc: Ensemble drama about conversations overheard in a bistro: two chess players see unfolding dramas, a couple on an uncomfortable blind date, a crumbling marriage, and film-noir fans that think they're witnessing a real-life murder.

programme.title: Citizen Duane
programme.desc: CITIZEN DUANE is a comedy/drama about Duane Balfour a teen-aged Don Quixote born into a family of spectacular failure. What starts as a simple schoolyard rivalry snowballs out of control when Duane decides to run for mayor of the tiny town of Ridgeway. If Duane is to succeed, he must not only overcome the powerful incumbents, but also his own inadequacies, public perception, and history itself.

programme.title: Comedy Meets Classic
programme.desc: Created by British comedy duo Carrington-Brown, based in Berlin, and Irish conductor ClA�odhna NA� AodA�in, based in Switzerland. They join forces with "The Swonderful Orchestra" for this exciting, classy, and hilarious music & comedy show.

programme.title: Flirting With Flamenco
programme.desc: When Sylvia's well-meaning dad (Watt) surprises her with a devastating revelation, Sylvia's world is turned upside down. But will she crumble or prove herself at the local flamenco contest? An uplifting feel-good Brit comedy drama, Flirting with Flamenco will have you laughing, crying and feeling empowered to turn your life around.

programme.title: Citizen Duane
programme.desc: CITIZEN DUANE is a comedy/drama about Duane Balfour a teen-aged Don Quixote born into a family of spectacular failure. What starts as a simple schoolyard rivalry snowballs out of control when Duane decides to run for mayor of the tiny town of Ridgeway. If Duane is to succeed, he must not only overcome the powerful incumbents, but also his own inadequacies, public perception, and history itself.

programme.title: The Flying Deuces
programme.desc: When two bumbling friends join the French Foreign Legion on a whim, they find themselves in a whirlwind of misadventures, love, and laughter as they attempt to navigate the challenges of military life in a foreign land.

programme.title: Perfect Girl
programme.desc: A coming of age romance for anyone who's ever had a crush. Since high school, Stan and Jenny have had crushes on each other. They wrote letters to one another over school holidays but in person they barely spoke; sharing only the occasional lingering glance and smile. Over the years they fantasized about how perfect they would be as lovers. Ten years later they bump into each other and have the chance to make it a reality, but it's not that simple; self doubt, fear of rejection, of losing their fantasies will hold them back from what could be the perfect union.

programme.title: I Would Have Kissed You
programme.desc: Three months after college graduation, best friends Mattie and Olivia are struggling to write a feature and struggling even more with their love lives. Mattie finds herself in a grey area with her college ex-boyfriend while Olivia clings to the hope that her crush will finally want to be with her (despite his hot new girlfriend.) British Web Awards - Awarded "Best Writing in a Dramedy" and "Best Music" Top Indie Awards -Awarded "Best Humor" WRPN Women's International Film Festival - Awarded "Exceptional Merit Award"

programme.title: The General
programme.desc: When Union spies steal Johnnie Gray's (Buster Keaton) beloved locomotive, the General, he pursues them with the aid of his fiance, Annabelle Lee (Marion Mack) straight through enemy lines. One of the most revered comedies of the silent era.

programme.title: Finding Joy
programme.desc: A struggling writer rediscovers himself, his offbeat family, and what it means to be happy when he meets Joy – a spirited, possibly-dying young woman who asks him to write her obituary.

programme.title: Brazzy Jazzy
programme.desc: When a Brazilian Girl takes on the NYC fashion world, her adventures are sometimes sexy, often funny but always Caffeinated! It's Jane the Virgin meets Girls, only an outsider immigrant version - more like Girls of the 3rd World.

programme.title: Growing Op
programme.desc: In an average American neighborhood, a family of four breaks all conformity making it difficult for their 18 year old son to fit in to society.

programme.title: 30 Nights of Sex
programme.desc: In a last ditch effort to save their marriage, Nick and Willa visit a renowned, yet eccentric, couples therapist and embark on a month-long journey of provocative and hilarious sex assignments.

The debate rages…on Xploration Outer Space.

programme.title: Xploration Outer Space - Shifting Sands
programme.desc: The last man to walk on the moon was Gene Cernan on the Apollo 17 mission, in 1972. He said, “As we leave the moon, we leave as we came and God willing as we shall return. ”But with Nasa relying on government funding, the path back to the moon has been full of obstacles. This episode examines how each new President has their own vision of space exploration, and why this results in stops and starts in the space program.

programme.title: Whaddyado - Sailing Team
programme.desc: A picture perfect photo opportunity turns nearly tragic in a flash. A young boy is home alone when two intruders break in to his house. Racing in the Gulf of Mexico puts a sailing team in deep trouble. And our moral dilemma looks at the lure of internet gambling.

programme.title: Whaddyado - Avalanche
programme.desc: A snowmobile rider goes mountain climbing and starts an avalanche. * We revisit the Mount St. Helen eruption site and hear from those who survived the volcano. * A house boat gets stuck on a dam on the Kentucky River. * A woman kayaker is pinned against a rock in a rapid. Will she survive?

programme.title: Whaddyado - Athlete Collapses
programme.desc: A boy catches fire and a young onlooker has what it takes to tackle the situation. * An athlete collapses in the weight room and a race against the clock begins trying to revive him. * A moral dilemma segment examines an inappropriate teacher-student relationship.

programme.title: ChatRoom - Self Cutting
programme.desc: An adult host and a panel of four young adults discuss dilemmas, scenarios and situations that are relevant to kids' lives. This week’s topics include: She’s taken control of their relationship and now things are out of control. And your friend seems to be intentionally injuring herself. How would you handle it?

programme.title: ChatRoom - Dad's Dating
programme.desc: An adult host and a panel of four young adults discuss dilemmas, scenarios and situations that are relevant to kids' lives. This week’s topics include: Her boyfriend is all hands and it’s making her uncomfortable. Also, mom died and now dad’s dating – how do you feel about it?

programme.title: ChatRoom - Teacher / Student
programme.desc: ChatRoom focuses on the ever-changing issues for today’s teens in a format that invites viewers to listen in on the conversation. This week’s topics include: What are the implications when a teacher makes a pass at a student? And “Sexting” sounds exciting but there’s a lot to consider before you hit send.

programme.title: Awesome Adventures - Brazil
programme.desc: The South American country of Brazil serves as the backdrop for our adventures this week. On day one we experience Avorismo, a trip that begins with tree climbing and ends with a splash. Day two starts with Olodum, a Brazilian percussion session that we beat like a drum and we take in Projeto Tamar to learn all about the varieties of sea turtles that call Brazil home. We shake things up on day three as we learn how to dance the samba then visit the city and experience the culture of Salvador, Bahia. We finish our adventures by training in the Brazilian martial art of Capoeria and leave things up in the air as we try our hand at juggling.

programme.title: Awesome Adventures - Quebec
programme.desc: On this week’s show we’ll visit Quebec City, Quebec. First, we’ll visit the Citadel and experience what it’s like to be a cadet. Then we’re off to learn all there is to know about maple sugaring. Next, we go on a bee safari and discover things we didn’t know about bees. Then, we’ll try yachting. To wrap up the show, we have some fun go-carting.

programme.title: Awesome Adventures - Las Vegas
programme.desc: This week’s “Awesome Adventure” takes place in the city of Las Vegas. We’ll attempt a unique type of skydiving…one that takes place indoors. Then we’ll head outdoors taking to the sky in some old fashioned WW II biplanes. We’ll visit the world famous Hoover Dam and then we’ll meet up with some circus folk and learn a few tricks of the trade. Finally, we’ll visit Lake Mead for a jet skiing adventure, and the Valley of Fire for some four wheelin’ fun.

programme.title: Wild About Animals - Powerful Predators
programme.desc: This show is dedicated to some of the world’s most powerful predators- from sharks in the Gulf of Mexico, to eagles and wolves in Minnesota. We’ll also explore the controversial topic of whether large predators should be kept in captivity in places like Zoo’s and SeaWorld.

programme.title: Wild About Animals - Canned Hunting
programme.desc: Come visit a college in southern California that teaches courses like Exotic Animal Training to prospective animal trainers. Then, look at the gruesome, but legal sport of canned hunting. And don’t forget that many victims of natural disasters are animals, often left behind to fend for themselves or perish. Now, the Humane Society offers to help pets in need when disaster strikes. Finally we’ll see the Shambala preserve, a haven for endangered, exotic big cats.

programme.title: Wild About Animals - Yellowstone
programme.desc: This week we’ll travel to Yellowstone National Park and visit the animals that inhabit this national wonder. We’ll also meet photographers Russ Finley and Tom Murphy, who make a living out in the wild. Then learn more about the dog’s canine cousins the wolf and the coyote.

programme.title: Whaddyado - Car Fire
programme.desc: A routine trip to visit some relatives literally takes a turn for the worse. *A trooper arrives on the scene of a car fire and someone’s trapped inside the burning vehicle. *A young man’s car is immobilized by rapidly rising water and he can’t open the door.*A woman pulls into her driveway and catches a burglar in the act.

programme.title: Whaddyado - Car Fall
programme.desc: A car falls on a man’s chest and his teenage nephew must find the strength to help solve this weighty problem and save his uncle’s life. * A bicycle brake impales a young boy’s leg and the resulting wound is more serious than anyone thought. * A moral dilemma segment deals with how to handle a stalker.

programme.title: Whaddyado - Kitchen Fire
programme.desc: * The son of a firefighter proves he can stand the heat in a kitchen on fire.* A young girl pulls off a great escape when she fights off an ex-con trying to abduct her. * This week we take a closer look at the alarming trend of cutting or self-injury among teens

programme.title: ChatRoom - Stalking
programme.desc: An adult host and a panel of four young adults discuss dilemmas, scenarios and situations that are relevant to kids' lives. This week’s topics include: Someone is stalking you. How do you handle it? And what happens if you don’t get into the college of your choice?

programme.title: ChatRoom - Cyber Bully
programme.desc: An adult host and a panel of four young adults discuss dilemmas, scenarios and situations that are relevant to kids' lives. This week’s topics include: A coach who takes motivation to the extreme. And cyber bullying is becoming more and more common. What can you do about it?

programme.title: ChatRoom - Bad Mother
programme.desc: This week’s topics include: He seems familiar, but will he take them for a ride? And Mom makes an offer that could change the whole party. Is she a cool mom or a poor parent? If teens are thinking about it or feeling it, we’re discussing it, in the ChatRoom.

programme.title: Awesome Adventures - Islands
programme.desc: On this week’s “Awesome Adventures,” we’ll travel to the Bahamas to watch a trained troop of flamingos, visit an 18th century fort, and learn how to make a traditional Bahamian dish. We’ll experience the adventure of a lifetime as we venture into shark-infested waters. Then we’ll learn all about sailing as we hit the open waters.

programme.title: Iceland
programme.desc: Bundle up because this week Nicole explores Iceland for a few days of winter!

programme.title: Awesome Adventures - Thailand
programme.desc: This week we head to Southeast Asia to spend time in Phuket, Thailand.

programme.title: Wild About Animals - Best of 1996
programme.desc: This episode features the best of 1996/1997 season. From the underwater world of the Great Barrier Reef to the Serengeti in Africa, visit the extraordinary places and animals highlighted in this presentation of “Wild About Animals.”

programme.title: Wild About Animals - Alaska Raven
programme.desc: On this episode of “Wild About Animals,” we’ll watch as one man wrestles alligators for a living. We’ll go to Anchorage, Alaska to find out the truth about the mysterious raven. Then, we’ll look at a sport for dogs that requires athletic ability and teamwork that some say is the ultimate game of fetch. The sport is called flyball, and all kinds of dogs just love it. And we’ll visit a place that rescues, rehabilitates and releases injured seals and sea lions.

programme.title: Countdown To Apollo - Factor Fiction
programme.desc: This episode examines some of the popular notions surrounding the Apollo program and discerns whether they are fact or fiction. These include: were Neil Armstrong’s words when he stepped on the moon scripted by Nasa? Products such as Velcro and Teflon are thought to be invented during the space program: true or false? Did President Kennedy try to work together with the Soviet Union to get a man on the moon? These and more are featured in Fact or Fiction.

programme.title: Countdown To Apollo - Amiable Strangers
programme.desc: Three very different, uniquely talented men came together to form the crew of Apollo 11. Neil Armstrong, the skilled pilot, Buzz Aldrin, the astronaut with a PhD, and Mike Collins, the well-liked pilot of the command module. This episode looks at all three men, not only in their professional capacities, but their personalities as well. They were, as Mike Collins described them, “amiable strangers.”

programme.title: The Apollo Chronicles - Part 2 - Perilous Steps
programme.desc: The Gemini program is a crucial stepping stone on the path to the Moon.

programme.desc: Host Steve Spangler and his sidekick Higginsworth return to the Museum of Science, Boston, where they take simple demonstrations they’ve done on DIY Sci and make them gigantic! Higgins becomes a human-sized balancing toy and Steve get locked in a cage that’s struck by lightning at the world’s largest Van de Graaf generator.

programme.title: DIY Sci - Bet You Can't
programme.desc: Steve Spangler reveals amazing science tricks that will have you saying to your friends, “I bet you can’t do that!” He’ll show you tricks like how to balance a quarter on the edge of a dollar bill and how to stick your entire head through a hole in a small index card.

programme.title: Nature Knows Best - Bio-Building
programme.desc: Danni Washington, tours the "living building" known as the Bullit Cente.

programme.title: Nature Knows Best - Power Of Nature
programme.desc: Everything uses energy but humans are the only species destroying our planet to create it.

programme.title: Xploration Awesome Planet - Animal Rescues
programme.desc: In this episode, we will visit a few different animal rescues centers starting with the marine mammal centre in Vancouver as they tend to orphaned harbor seals.

programme.title: Xploration Awesome Planet - Student Explorer 2020
programme.desc: In this episode, we reveal the winner of our third ever #StudentExplorer Contest.

programme.title: Xploration Outer Space - The Search for Life
programme.desc: The search for life in the universe remains one of the most ambitious quests of humankind. Host Emily Calandrelli explores the possibility that life exists in our own celestial backyard

programme.title: Xploration Outer Space - UFOs: What’s Really Out There?
programme.desc: Is there proof that aliens are visiting our planet? What is behind these UFO sightings? Host Emily Calandrelli searches for the truth by interviewing experts and visiting Roswell, New Mexico, the site where some believe aliens once landed.

programme.title: Life 2.0 - Drones Away
programme.desc: In this episode we explore some of the newest and most innovative uses for drones and reveal how they are becoming increasingly ubiquitous. Much like how the automobile once changed the world, drones are poised to do the same. Could we end up in a society where it’s normal to look up and see the sky abuzz with activity?

programme.desc: This episode looks at how virtual reality will transform our lives.

programme.desc: Steve Spangler shows you toys you can make at home, all based on science.

programme.title: DIY Sci - Backyard Science
programme.desc: Steve Spangler relaxes in his backyard with science tricks and inventions you can create outdoors.

programme.desc: Every species found in nature is a survivor, there’s a reason they’ve been here this long.

programme.title: Nature Knows Best - Whirlybird
programme.desc: Helicopters took a lot of their early inspiration from one of nature’s most efficient fliers.

programme.desc: Philippe Cousteau meets with incredible students across the country who are solving real problems.

programme.title: Xploration Awesome Planet - Marvels Of Nature
programme.desc: Philippe Cousteau explores unbelievable marvels of nature across our awesome planet.

programme.title: Xploration Outer Space - Shifting Sands
programme.desc: The last man to walk on the moon was Gene Cernan on the Apollo 17 mission, in 1972. He said, “As we leave the moon, we leave as we came and God willing as we shall return. ”But with Nasa relying on government funding, the path back to the moon has been full of obstacles. This episode examines how each new President has their own vision of space exploration, and why this results in stops and starts in the space program.

programme.title: Xploration Outer Space - Moon to Mars
programme.desc: The moon is the next logical starting point for deep space exploration, and the Artemis missions are headed there. But there are those who think it is a mistake to focus on our closet celestial neighbor. They say we should get to Mars, and once there, turn it into a living planet. The debate rages…on Xploration Outer Space.
